title: ASAP: an Agentic Solution to Auto-optimize Performance of Large-Scale LLM Training

mechanism.populationDetail: The system starts from one baseline experiment and stores worklog/history context, but does not maintain an explicit evolving population of candidate configurations.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The past-optimization database and Sharding Memory provide retrieval and traceability context, not a current elite archive with archive admission.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Three proposals are generated for human or hardware review; an Evaluator Agent and closed feedback/reinforcement loop are future work, so no current survivor or replacement rule is defined.
mechanism.generationDetail: The Proposal Agent generates new sharding configurations from task/profiling/analyzer/retrieval context without directly editing a selected parent candidate.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Profiler metadata and Analyzer diagnosis guide proposal generation but are not described as feedback returned alongside an evaluated candidate's score; closed-loop evaluation is future work.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: No true evolutionary parent is selected. The baseline experiment/configuration conditions the prompt, while similar historical optimization records are retrieved as contextual references.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Agentic RAG recommendation over system configurations with persistent worklog and external historical retrieval, but without an explicit evolving candidate population, evaluator, or replacement loop.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/ASAP an Agentic Solution to Auto-optimize Performance of Large-Scale LLM Training.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Do not infer an elite archive, replacement mechanism, true parent, or explicit adaptive explore-exploit policy from the historical database, Sharding Memory, or three proposed alternatives. The survey cites ASAP for memory-only population, prompt context/roles, zero-parent generation, and semantic-similarity reference reuse; evaluator-feedback and explore-exploit placement should remain absent unless the taxonomy is intentionally broadened.
